Alarms

No alarm stands now. After each collect, every five minutes, the readings are looked at for six things. An alarm goes into the journal, onto the rig's charts as a mark, and to whoever watches the rigs; its end goes into the journal too.

alarmraised by
Rounds stalla node that has neither finished a round, nor stopped, nor started again for 3 times its usual round (the median of its last 10, or its last if that took longer), and at least 3 minutes; after a start, 20 minutes for the first round; a node at rest between its rounds, its night, gets 3 times its round and its rest, and 10 minutes at least; and a node whose process is gone without a clean stop is raised after 3 minutes
A rig is silenta rig that has not answered the collector for 10 minutes, or answers but has sent no reading for as long
Organisms falla node's organisms falling by more than half within 10 rounds, or within 10 minutes where its rounds are shorter than a minute, from 100,000 or more
The drive fillsfree space on the world's drive under the reserve the node keeps; below it the node makes no new land
A guard stopped a nodea node that its guard has stopped cleanly, because its rig ran out of memory or lost its network, and that has not been started since: nothing starts it again by itself
The bus reports errorsa new error on a rig's links to its chips and cards (PCI Express), by the kernel's own count, whether the hardware corrected it or not: a rig's usual count is none. It stands while new errors come within 10 minutes. On 12 November 2026 such errors rose for 20 to 50 minutes before a rig lost the link to its chipset, twice

Read from the kernel's counters and one query of the graphics driver a minute; the drives' wear from their own logs. "Cards: computing" is the node's own count of the seconds a card worked in a round; "busy when read" is what the driver said at the moment of a reading, and the two need not agree. Under rules 7 each node reads what its own device draws, the processor too, and that is the light of its band; the power of the rest of the machines is not measured.
